paper.title_en: Pairing connections between localized nuclear regions: Orbital reweighting and thermal quenching
paper.abstract_en: The nucleon localization function (NLF) characterizes nuclear spatial structure; the nonlocal anomalous density (pairing tensor) describes coherent pair amplitude between two points. Global pairing measures leave connections between distinct spatial regions unresolved. We determine how selective orbital participation strengthens pairing connections between localized regions during overall pairing loss, and why heating attenuates the connection while preserving its pattern. Axial Hartree-Fock plus BCS calculations combine NLF with the pairing tensor in shape-constrained 20Ne (distinct localization lobes) and octupole-deformed 144Ba (reflection-asymmetric background). Complete signed orbital sums separate anomalous-weight and spatial-kernel changes at fixed pairing strength and cutoff. Contraction along a constrained 20Ne branch preserves identifiable end lobes while reducing total anomalous norm and increasing the absolute opposite-end integral. Coupled spectrum and gap changes favor a mixed 1d5/2/2s1/2 component and deplete anomalous participation of a predominantly 1p1/2 component. Increased positive strength and weaker destructive interference overcome the net opposing spatial-kernel response; this balance survives mesh refinement. Heating at the reference quadrupole constraint yields compensating thermal and quasiparticle-energy factors, so similar gap reductions produce nearly common attenuation. In 144Ba, octupole deformation and normal-localization modulation persist after anomalous sources vanish. Regional enhancement depends on how selective anomalous participation changes the complete signed orbital sum, including spatial feedback. Nearly proportional participation changes preserve the pattern when kernels remain stable, distinguishing stronger absolute connections from larger normalized fractions on an identifiable localization background.
